dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003estuntd is a local, self-hosted proxy that records the typed decisions your app already makes and\nlearns to answer them itself.\u003c/strong\u003e It speaks the Jev System One protocol (\u003ccode\u003ePOST /v1/systemone\u003c/code\u003e, with\n\u003ccode\u003echoice\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003escore\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003enoul\u003c/code\u003e questions) and the OpenAI Chat Completions API, distils each decision\nsite into a small head on a frozen \u003ca href=\"https://huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eLaya\u003c/a\u003e encoder,\nand serves that answer locally with calibrated confidence, handing anything it is unsure about back\nto the provider.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTry it in the browser:\u003c/strong\u003e the \u003ca href=\"https://huggingface.co/spaces/pollix/stuntd\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eHugging Face Space\u003c/a\u003e\nputs zero-shot Laya and the heads stuntd trained side by side on three demos, no install.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThree ways to run it:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLocal Jev.\u003c/strong\u003e No key, no provider, no training. Point \u003ccode\u003etypesafe-sdk\u003c/code\u003e at stuntd and the base Laya\ncheckpoint answers your typed questions.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eIn front of OpenAI.\u003c/strong\u003e A drop-in replacement for the provider base URL. Typed requests are\nrecorded; everything else is relayed byte for byte.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eIn front of the paid Jev API.\u003c/strong\u003e stuntd relays, learns from the provider's own answers, and\ntakes the decision over once its head is right often enough.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eStatus: early release, v0.1. Every number below traces to a demo in this repository or to a source\nlisted at the end.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWho it is for\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-who-it-is-for\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Who it is for\" href=\"#who-it-is-for\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eYou have no Jev key.\u003c/strong\u003e TypeSafe's Jev is an early-access API at the time of writing, and there\nare no published weights. stuntd answers the same typed questions locally on Laya, with no key\nand no training, so a \u003ccode\u003etypesafe-sdk\u003c/code\u003e client keeps working while you wait.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eYou pay a provider for the same decision thousands of times a day.\u003c/strong\u003e Routing, triage,\nmoderation, gating. stuntd distils those answers into a local head: tens of milliseconds, no\ntokens, no round trip.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eZero-shot Laya is not good enough on your labels.\u003c/strong\u003e On banking77's 77 intents it scores 38.2\nwhere Jev scores 76.4. A few thousand rows of your own traffic is what closes that gap: in the\nbanking demo the risk question goes from 30.0% to 72.5%.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eYou want a Claude Code hook that decides locally.\u003c/strong\u003e A \u003ccode\u003ePreToolUse\u003c/code\u003e gate answering \"may this\ncommand run\" in about 50 ms, without sending every command you type to a provider.\n\u003ca href=\"/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/examples/devtools\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eexamples/devtools/\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e ships the hook.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eQuickstart: local Jev without an API typesafe_sdk import Choice, Noul, TypeSafeClient\n\nQUESTIONS = {\n    \u0026quot;category\u0026quot;: Choice(\n        instructions=\u0026quot;Which part of the product is this ticket about?\u0026quot;,\n        criteria={\u0026quot;billing\u0026quot;: \u0026quot;Payments and refunds.\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;bug\u0026quot;: \u0026quot;Something is broken.\u0026quot;},\n    ),\n    \u0026quot;needs_human\u0026quot;: Noul(instructions=\u0026quot;Does a support agent have to read this?\u0026quot;),\n}\n\nwith TypeSafeClient(api_key=\u0026quot;local\u0026quot;, base_url=\u0026quot;http://127.0.0.1:8787\u0026quot;) as client:\n    answer = client.system_one(\n        state={\u0026quot;subject\u0026quot;: \u0026quot;Charged twice\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;body\u0026quot;: \u0026quot;Two identical charges on Friday.\u0026quot;},\n        questions=QUESTIONS,\n    )\nprint(answer.choices[\u0026quot;category\u0026quot;].choice, answer.nouls[\u0026quot;needs_human\u0026quot;].noul)\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003efrom\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-s1\"\u003etypesafe_sdk\u003c/span\u003e class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\"category\"\u003c/span\u003e: \u003cspan class=\"pl-en\"\u003eChoice\u003c/span\u003e(\n        \u003cspan class=\"pl-s1\"\u003einstructions\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003e=\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\"Which part of the product is this ticket about?\"\u003c/span\u003e,\n        \u003cspan class=\"pl-s1\"\u003ecriteria\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003e=\u003c/span\u003e{\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\"billing\"\u003c/span\u003e: \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\"Payments and refunds.\"\u003c/span\u003e, \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\"bug\"\u003c/span\u003e: \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\"Something is broken.\"\u003c/span\u003e},\n    ),\n    \u003cspan protocol plugs in the same way, by changing one base URL wherever the\nclient exposes it: \u003ccode\u003etypesafe-sdk\u003c/code\u003e, JevRouter, the local-server request of fast-jev-compaction, and\nthe browser and game agents built on the same SDK.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe key is ignored unless you set \u003ccode\u003e[jev] require_key = true\u003c/code\u003e. dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--upstream\u003c/code\u003e is the provider origin only, without \u003ccode\u003e/v1\u003c/code\u003e: your client's own path is appended to it\nunchanged. In the client, point \u003ccode\u003ebase_url\u003c/code\u003e at the daemon:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"import os\n\nfrom openai import OpenAI\n\nclient = OpenAI(base_url=\u0026quot;http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1\u0026quot;, api_key=os.environ[\u0026quot;OPENAI_API_KEY\u0026quot;])\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eimport\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-s1\"\u003eos\u003c/span\u003e\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003efrom\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-s1\"\u003eopenai\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eimport\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-v\"\u003eOpenAI\u003c/span\u003e\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-s1\"\u003eclient\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003e=\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-en\"\u003eOpenAI\u003c/span\u003e(\u003cspan class=\"pl-s1\"\u003ebase_url\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003e=\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\"http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1\"\u003c/span\u003e, \u003cspan class=\"pl-s1\"\u003eapi_key\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003e=\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-s1\"\u003eos\u003c/span\u003e.\u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003eenviron\u003c/span\u003e[\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\"OPENAI_API_KEY\"\u003c/span\u003e])\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEverything keeps working exactly as before. A request whose \u003ccode\u003eresponse_format\u003c/code\u003e (or single tool) asks\nfor an object with one enum, boolean or number field is a typed decision, and stuntd records it\nwith the provider's answer. Anything else is relayed untouched, streaming included.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOnce a site has a few hundred captures:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"stuntd status                  # what has been recorded, per site\nstuntd train                   # one head per site with enough examples\nstuntd report                  # holdout agreement, ECE, the operating point\nstuntd enable \u0026lt;site\u0026gt;           # let that site answer locally\"\u003e\u003cpre href=\"/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/docs/before-after.svg\"\u003e\u003cimg src=\"/bladedevoff/stuntd/raw/main/docs/before-after.svg\" alt=\"Accuracy against the teacher, before and after training, per decision site\" style=\"max-width: 100%;\"\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSnake is scored by what the answers do rather than by how many of them are right:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ca target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" href=\"/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/docs/snake.svg\"\u003e\u003cimg 100%;\"\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFive of the seven sites in the three text demos reach a holdout agreement of 0.95 or better. The\ndemos run at the default \u003ccode\u003etarget_agreement\u003c/code\u003e of 0.99, which picks each head's operating point rather\nthan being a score it reached. The two that fall short, support's \u003ccode\u003eurgency\u003c/code\u003e at 0.935 and banking's\n\u003ccode\u003erisk\u003c/code\u003e at 0.937, stay in the demos anyway: see \u003ca href=\"#limitations\"\u003elimitations\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eLatency, size and cost:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003e\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003emeasured\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eone head answer on CUDA\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003ep50 22 ms, 26 ms in process\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003ethe same head on CPU\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e60 to 62 ms\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eone live answer through the daemon, over TCP\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e28 ms\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003ewhat the relay itself adds when the provider answers\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e2.1 ms\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eJev API round trip, through OpenRouter\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003ep50 376 to 389 ms\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eJev price\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e$0.042 per 1M input tokens, output free\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003etraining one head: 5890 rows, 24 epochs\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e186 s\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003etraining three heads: 3000 rows each, 24 epochs\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e362 s\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003ea trained head on disk\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eabout 50 MB, fp16\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe first four rows were measured during development on an RTX 5060 laptop running Windows. They\ncome from no published benchmark, and there is no link to give for them. The two training rows are\nthe Snake and support demos of this repository, on the same laptop with the encoder cache on; the\ndevtools demo measured the same 24-epoch run at 730 s with the cache off against 231 s with it on,\n3.2x.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhy train at all, rather than run Laya zero-shot. From\n\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/dhruvmehra/jevbench\"\u003ejevbench\u003c/a\u003e, n=500 per dataset, accuracy:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003edataset\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003elabels\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eLaya zero-shot\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eJev\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003efine-tuned DistilBERT\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003esst2\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e2\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e92.0\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e95.4\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e91.0\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eagnews\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e4\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e90.6\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e84.3\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e91.0\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003ebanking77\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e77\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e38.2\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e76.4\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e88.0\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eZero-shot Laya holds its own at two or four labels and collapses at seventy-seven. A model trained\non a few thousand of your own examples does not: that is the bet stuntd makes, and the four demos\nare what it is measured against.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eHow stuntd distils decisions into a Laya head\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-how-stuntd-distils-decisions-into-a-laya-head\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: How stuntd distils decisions into a Laya head\" href=\"#how-stuntd-distils-decisions-into-a-laya-head\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"   your app\n      |\n      v\n  +-------------------------------------------------+\n  |  stuntd                                          |\n  |                                                  |\n  |   typed decision?  -- no ---------------------------\u0026gt;  provider, byte for byte\n  |         |                                        |\n  |        yes                                       |\n  |         v                                        |\n  |   head confident?  -- yes --\u0026gt;  local answer      |     20 to 100 ms, no tokens\n  |         |                                        |\n  |         no, or a 2% check sample                 |\n  +---------|----------------------------------------+\n            v\n        provider  (answer returned to the caller, and recorded as a capture)\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e   your app\n      |\n      v\n  +-------------------------------------------------+\n  |  stuntd                                          |\n  |                                                  |\n  |   typed decision?  -- no ---------------------------\u0026gt;  provider, byte for byte\n  |         |                                        |\n  |        yes                                       |\n  |         v                                        |\n  |   head confident?  -- yes --\u0026gt;  local answer      |     20 to 100 ms, no tokens\n  |         |                                        |\n  |         no, or a 2% check sample                 |\n  +---------|----------------------------------------+\n            v\n        provider  (answer returned to the caller, and recorded as a capture)\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA \u003cstrong\u003edecision site\u003c/strong\u003e is one place in your code that makes one decision. On the Jev path the site is\nthe question's name. On the OpenAI path it is a hash of the response schema and the system prompt,\nor whatever you put in the \u003ccode\u003eX-Stuntd-Site\u003c/code\u003e request header.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eKeep one decision to a question. A question that mixes two, such as \"is it urgent and which team\nhandles it\", learns worse than two separate questions.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEach site walks through four modes.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ecollect.\u003c/strong\u003e The provider answers everything. stuntd stores the request text and the answer,\nwith the redaction rules applied before anything is written.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003etrain.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003estuntd train\u003c/code\u003e fits one classification head per site on the frozen Laya encoder,\nholds back 20% of the rows, and reports the holdout agreement, the calibration error and the\nconfidence threshold at which the head reaches your \u003ccode\u003etarget_agreement\u003c/code\u003e:\n\u003ccode\u003ecategory  trained  holdout agreement 0.992  coverage 1.00 at agreement 0.992  ece 0.024\u003c/code\u003e.\nBelow that threshold the head abstains, which is what coverage measures: the share of requests\nit is willing to answer at all. \u003ccode\u003estuntd enable\u003c/code\u003e refuses a head whose coverage rounds to zero and\nwarns below 10%.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eshadow.\u003c/strong\u003e The caller still gets the provider's answer; the head answers beside it and the two\nare compared. \u003ccode\u003estuntd status\u003c/code\u003e shows the running agreement.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003elive.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003estuntd enable \u0026lt;site\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e and the head answers the caller. Anything under the threshold\nstill goes to the provider. So does a \u003ccode\u003echeck_share\u003c/code\u003e sample, 2% by default, and those samples are\nwhat keeps the head honest: once agreement over the last \u003ccode\u003ewindow\u003c/code\u003e decisions falls below\n\u003ccode\u003etarget_agreement\u003c/code\u003e, the site demotes itself back to shadow and logs why. Promotion the other way\nis manual unless you set \u003ccode\u003eserving.auto_promote\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIn proxy mode the provider behind \u003ccode\u003e[jev] upstream\u003c/code\u003e does not have to be the paid API. Any server\nthat speaks \u003ccode\u003ePOST /v1/systemone\u003c/code\u003e can sit there -- kev, LLM2Jev, the laya-server family -- which\nmakes it a keyless local teacher: it answers, stuntd records, and the head learns from it.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eNothing is uploaded. Captures live in a SQLite file under your user directory with private\npermissions, and there is no telemetry.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eChecking a head against verified rows\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-checking-a-head-against-verified-rows\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Checking a head against verified rows\" href=\"#checking-a-head-against-verified-rows\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAgreement measures how faithfully a head copies its teacher, the teacher's mistakes included. It\nsays nothing about whether either of them is right. For that, write a few hundred rows a person\nhas checked, in the same JSONL format \u003ccode\u003estuntd import\u003c/code\u003e reads, and score the site against them:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"stuntd report \u0026lt;site\u0026gt; --gold verified.jsonl\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003estuntd report \u0026lt;site\u0026gt; --gold verified.jsonl\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor example:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"site tickets  gold rows 300: 296 used, 4 skipped\nhead accuracy 0.892\nhead accuracy 0.875 on 8 rows the store has not seen\nserved accuracy 0.936 at threshold 0.62: 71% answered locally, 3 below it with no teacher answer\nteacher accuracy 0.948 on 288 rows\nhead and teacher: both right 252, both wrong 10, head only 5, teacher only 21\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003esite tickets  gold rows 300: 296 used, 4 skipped\nhead accuracy 0.892\nhead accuracy 0.875 on 8 rows the store has not seen\nserved accuracy 0.936 at threshold 0.62: 71% answered locally, 3 below it with no teacher answer\nteacher accuracy 0.948 on 288 rows\nhead and teacher: both right 252, both wrong 10, head only 5, teacher only 21\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe head answers every row. The teacher's answer is the latest capture of that exact text, so it\nis there only for rows stuntd has already seen, and those are rows the head may have trained on.\nThe line for rows the store has not seen is the out-of-sample number, so do not import the gold\nrows or send them through the proxy before scoring. Served accuracy is what stuntd would serve\nonce the site is live: the head at or above the threshold, the teacher below it. Rows whose answer\nis not one of the site's labels are skipped. \u003ccode\u003e--json\u003c/code\u003e prints the same numbers, and the command needs the train\nextra, since it loads the base model.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003eX-Stuntd\u003c/code\u003e header\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-the-x-stuntd-header\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: The X-Stuntd header\" href=\"#the-x-stuntd-header\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEvery answer says how it was served, so a silent fallback cannot hide.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOn the OpenAI path: the mode, then the fields that apply.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"X-Stuntd: live; site=moderation; confidence=0.97\nX-Stuntd: collect; site=moderation; reason=low-confidence\nX-Stuntd: passthrough; reason=no-schema\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eX-Stuntd: live; site=moderation; confidence=0.97\nX-Stuntd: collect; site=moderation; reason=low-confidence\nX-Stuntd: passthrough; \u003ccode\u003eshadow\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecollect\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003echeck\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eretrained\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003emodel-error\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eno-runtime\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estate-error\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eupstream-error\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOn the Jev (no Jev provider behind it) or \u003ccode\u003eproxy\u003c/code\u003e (the paid API is)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003equestions=\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003ehow many questions the request asked\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003elive=\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eanswered by a trained head\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eshadow=\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003esite in shadow mode, proxy mode only\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezeroshot=\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eanswered by the base checkpoint, local mode only\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003elearn=off\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003elearn = false\u003c/code\u003e, so nothing was recorded\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ereason=\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eno-key\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ebad-request\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003enot-parsed\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eno-runtime\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003emodel-error\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eupstream-error\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" config show\u003c/code\u003e prints every setting with where it came\nfrom. Every key is optional and a missing one keeps the default.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003ekey\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003edefault\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003ewhat it does\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eupstream\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e\"\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eProvider origin the OpenAI path forwards to, no path. Empty: only the Jev routes are served.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ehost\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e127.0.0.1\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAddress the daemon listens on.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eport\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e8787\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003ePort the daemon listens on.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003elearn\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etrue\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWhether the daemon records anything at all. \u003ccode\u003efalse\u003c/code\u003e is a pure proxy, or a pure local Jev.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eredaction.enabled\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etrue\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eBuilt-in email and phone rules run before a capture is written.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eredaction.patterns\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e[]\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eExtra regular expressions, each replaced with \u003ccode\u003e[redacted]\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estorage.db_path\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecaptures.sqlite\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eCapture database; a relative path resolves against the data directory.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estorage.max_rows\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e100000\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eCaptures kept before the oldest are pruned.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estorage.max_age_days\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e30\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAge at which a capture is pruned.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estorage.models_dir\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003emodels\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWhere trained heads live.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etraining.min_examples\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e300\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eCaptures a site needs before it is worth training.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etraining.holdout\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e0.2\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eShare of the rows held back to measure the head.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etraining.target_agreement\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e0.99\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAgreement with the teacher the head must reach; it sets the confidence threshold.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etraining.base_model\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003econvaiinnovations/laya\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eCheckpoint the heads are trained on. A local directory works too.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etraining.epochs\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e3\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003ePasses over the training rows. The demos use 24.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etraining.device\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eauto\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eauto\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecpu\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecuda\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003emps\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etraining.cache_encoder\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etrue\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWhether the frozen encoder runs once per example instead of once per epoch; off re-encodes.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etraining.cache_max_mb\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e0\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eMost memory the cached encoder output may take, in megabytes; 0 is half of physical memory. A bigger site trains uncached and says so on stderr.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etraining.max_option_tokens\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e1024\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eHow far a site with many or long labels may widen the option budget, in tokens, so every label is shown whole; past it, labels are cut short. A value below the checkpoint's own budget (192) keeps the checkpoint's.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eserving.check_share\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e0.02\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eShare of live requests still sent to the provider to check the head. Inert in local Jev mode.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eserving.window\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e100\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eRecent decisions a site is judged on.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eserving.min_window\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e20\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eDecisions needed before that judgement counts.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eserving.auto_promote\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003efalse\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWhether a shadow site that holds its target goes live on its own.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eserving.auto_promote_after_hours\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e24\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eHours in shadow before it may.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eserving.cache_size\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e1000\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAnswers kept in memory, one LRU cache shared by every site.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev.upstream\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e\"\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eOrigin of the paid Jev provider, no path. Empty: the base Laya answers locally.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev.require_key\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003efalse\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWhether a Jev request must carry a Bearer token. The token itself is not checked.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ejev.model_name\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estuntd\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eName reported in the \u003ccode\u003emodel\u003c/code\u003e field of a Jev answer.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cdiv table.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ca target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" href=\"/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/docs/snake-demo.gif\"\u003e\u003cimg src=\"/bladedevoff/stuntd/raw/main/docs/snake-demo.gif\" alt=\"Snake played three ways over the Jev protocol: base Laya zero-shot, the BFS teacher, and the head stuntd trained from the teacher's games\" data-animated-image=\"\" style=\"max-width: 100%;\"\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSame seed, same \u003ccode\u003etypesafe-sdk\u003c/code\u003e client, same daemon. Left: the base Laya checkpoint answering\nzero-shot. Middle: the BFS oracle that plays teacher. Right: the head stuntd trained from the\nteacher's 30 games (138 s), answering 99.6% of the moves itself at 20 ms each. Numbers and\ncommands are in \u003ca href=\"/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/examples/snake\"\u003eexamples/snake/\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/examples/snake\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eexamples/snake/\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e plays 12x12 Snake over the Jev protocol, one \u003ccode\u003echoice\u003c/code\u003e per\nmove. Zero-shot Laya scores 0.70 a game; the head scores 11.40 at \u003ccode\u003etarget_agreement = 0.95\u003c/code\u003e,\nanswering all but 13 of 3050 moves locally at a p50 of 21.1 ms. At the default 0.99 the same head\nscores 3.03 and answers 71% of the moves. That is the difference between \"let the head play\" and \"only when\nit is sure\", in one table.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/examples/support\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eexamples/support/\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e triages a helpdesk ticket with three questions in one\nrequest: \u003ccode\u003ecategory\u003c/code\u003e (choice), \u003ccode\u003eurgency\u003c/code\u003e (score) and \u003ccode\u003eneeds_human\u003c/code\u003e (noul). 90% of the questions\nend up answered locally.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/examples/banking\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eexamples/banking/\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e asks a banking intent over 12 labels and a payment risk\nverdict. 78% local, and \u003ccode\u003eintent\u003c/code\u003e reaches a holdout agreement of 1.000.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/examples/devtools\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eexamples/devtools/\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e gates a coding agent's shell command and calls a test\nfailure flaky. 98% local, and it ships the Claude Code \u003ccode\u003ePreToolUse\u003c/code\u003e hook that uses it.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThe teachers in all four are rules, not an LLM.\u003c/strong\u003e Three demos use a written rule over the\ngenerated text; Snake uses a BFS oracle. No Jev API key was available when these numbers were\ntaken, so the zero-shot rows are the base checkpoint, not the paid provider, and the same tables\nwith the real Jev API as the teacher have not been measured yet. What the demos do show is what a\nhead learns from a teacher that is consistent: the ceiling of the method, not of any one provider.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eLimitations\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-limitations\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Limitations\" href=\"#limitations\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThe encoder is frozen, so a head learns text, not arithmetic over fields.\u003c/strong\u003e This is the single\nmost important thing to know. In the banking demo the first version of the \u003ccode\u003erisk\u003c/code\u003e rule compared the\namount, the country and the hour numerically: the head reached 0.42 and covered 1% of the holdout.\nThe same decision, written as a sentence about the customer's own history, reaches 0.937 at\ncoverage 0.57. If your decision is really a calculation, write the calculation, not a model.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFree text is not a decision.\u003c/strong\u003e stuntd learns closed decisions only: an enum, a boolean or a\nnumber on the OpenAI path, \u003ccode\u003echoice\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003enoul\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003escore\u003c/code\u003e on the Jev path. A request that asks for\nprose, a summary or code is relayed and never recorded.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA site needs examples.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003etraining.min_examples\u003c/code\u003e is 300 and the demos use 3000 rows. A rare\ndecision, or one whose option list changes every week, is not a fit.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOverlapping labels make a head defer.\u003c/strong\u003e The weakest site of the three text demos is the\nsupport demo's \u003ccode\u003eurgency\u003c/code\u003e, a four-level \u003ccode\u003escore\u003c/code\u003e. Its levels overlap in wording, so the head\nreaches a 0.935 holdout agreement and answers 71% of the tickets at 99.1% agreement, handing the\nother 29% to the provider. That is a working site rather than a failure, but it is the shape to\nexpect when the labels are not cleanly separated by words.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOnly the OpenAI Chat Completions path learns.\u003c/strong\u003e Anthropic Messages, the OpenAI Responses API\nand Gemini pass through untouched. Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI run through stuntd as if\nit were not there.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eDetails worth knowing\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-details-worth-knowing\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Details worth knowing\" href=\"#details-worth-knowing\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSome decisions need more than the default 3 epochs.\u003c/strong\u003e The default stays 3, and the demos\ntrain at 24 because each of them measured what that bought. The frozen encoder runs once per\nsite and every epoch reads its cached output, so the extra epochs cost seconds, not minutes.\nAt 3 epochs the same sites answer almost nothing.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003escore\u003c/code\u003e takes 2 to 10 levels and \u003ccode\u003echoice\u003c/code\u003e takes at most 255 options.\u003c/strong\u003e Those are stuntd's own\nlimits, not a quotation from the Jev API. \u003ccode\u003einstructions\u003c/code\u003e is optional on a question.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA question name is a decision site.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003e:\u003c/code\u003e becomes \u003ccode\u003e.\u003c/code\u003e, so \u003ccode\u003ea:b\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003ea.b\u003c/code\u003e are one site. Two\nquestions with the same name but different criteria train one head on mixed data; give them\ndifferent names.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eGET /v1/models\u003c/code\u003e is answered by stuntd\u003c/strong\u003e, in the Jev shape, naming \u003ccode\u003ejev.model_name\u003c/code\u003e. In proxy\nmode it is relayed to the Jev provider. Either way an OpenAI client does not get the provider's\nmodel list through stuntd; every other \u003ccode\u003e/v1/models...\u003c/code\u003e path is relayed as usual.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLocal Jev mode compares nothing.\u003c/strong\u003e There is no second opinion to compare against, because the\nzero-shot answers come from the very checkpoint the head was distilled from. No request is\nsampled for a check, \u003ccode\u003estuntd status\u003c/code\u003e reports \u003ccode\u003e\"agreement\": null\u003c/code\u003e, and no site is ever demoted.\n\u003ccode\u003estuntd report\u003c/code\u003e, which measures the head against held-out rows, is the quality signal there. Put\na Jev provider in front and both come back.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOne CUDA workload at a time.\u003c/strong\u003e Stop the daemon before \u003ccode\u003estuntd train\u003c/code\u003e, or the two contend for\nthe same GPU.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEvery \u003ccode\u003eserve\u003c/code\u003e loads the base checkpoint\u003c/strong\u003e when \u003ccode\u003e[jev] upstream\u003c/code\u003e is empty, because local Jev\nanswers from it. The daemon runs one pass through the model before it accepts requests, so\nstartup costs seconds and the first request then runs close to the steady-state p50. Lazy\nloading is on the roadmap.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThe first start needs the network.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003eserve\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003etrain\u003c/code\u003e load \u003ccode\u003etraining.base_model\u003c/code\u003e, which\ndefaults to the Hub id, so the first run downloads the whole repository, the \u003ccode\u003emultilingual/\u003c/code\u003e\nand \u003ccode\u003etyped-decisions/\u003c/code\u003e checkpoints included. With \u003ccode\u003eHF_HUB_OFFLINE=1\u003c/code\u003e the Hub id loads only\nwhile that whole snapshot is in the Hugging Face cache; a partial one fails. For fully offline\nuse, set \u003ccode\u003etraining.base_model\u003c/code\u003e to a local directory holding the checkpoint, such as the\nsnapshot folder.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eCompared with\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-compared-with\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Compared with\" href=\"#compared-with\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/stiermid/laya-serve\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003estiermid/laya-serve\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/a\u003e is a Jev-compatible HTTP server\nfor Laya weights. It is the cleaner choice when zero-shot is all you want: it documents its\ndivergences from the Jev wire format carefully, and it carries no database, no training and no\nproxy. stuntd's local mode does the same job; what it adds is learning from traffic.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThe rest of the laya-server family serves those weights behind the same API:\n\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/noahbclarkson/laya-server\"\u003enoahbclarkson/laya-server\u003c/a\u003e ships a container, a\nhealth endpoint and TypeSafe's error shapes, \u003ca href=\"https://github.com/receptron/laya\"\u003ereceptron/laya\u003c/a\u003e\nruns Laya from Node through ONNX Runtime. All of them answer zero-shot only.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/jaredpalmer/kev\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ejaredpalmer/kev\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/a\u003e trains Jev-like decision models on\nQwen3.5 and publishes the weights at 0.8B, 4B and 9B, with the training code, frozen eval suites\nand a System One API in front of them. A whole model per decision, where stuntd trains one head\nper site on a frozen encoder.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/Yinsongxu/LLM2Jev\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eYinsongxu/LLM2Jev\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/a\u003e puts local LLMs behind\n\u003ccode\u003e/v1/systemone\u003c/code\u003e and scores each option during the prefill, so reordering the options does not\nchange the answer. stuntd has neither that order independence nor its image inputs; what it has\nis a head that answers without the LLM.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/TheoLeeCJ/SemIf\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTheoLeeCJ/SemIf\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/a\u003e reads typed option probabilities\nstraight out of open 4B models, with a browser demo and no waitlist. It reproduces the interface\nrather than the model, and every decision still costs a pass through the 4B.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/TianyuCodings/NanoJev\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTianyuCodings/NanoJev\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/a\u003e trains a 0.6B decision\nmodel from prepared game datasets and plays ViZDoom, a maze and Snake with the one checkpoint.\nIts Snake comes from a model trained for the game; stuntd's comes from a head distilled from\n5890 recorded moves of a BFS oracle.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/vinnylarouge/jevlike\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003evinnylarouge/jevlike\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/a\u003e trains an option-attention\nhead from JSONL rows of a context, its options and a label. That is \u003ccode\u003estuntd train\u003c/code\u003e as a\nstandalone library: you bring the rows, and nothing records them for you.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/gargpratyush/jev-router\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003egargpratyush/jev-router\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/a\u003e uses Jev to pick a\nmodel tier per turn for Claude Code and Codex. A different problem, and a good example of the\ndecision stuntd would learn: a routing call on every turn is exactly the repeated typed decision\nthat pays for a head.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/Santiago-j-s/jev-proxy\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSantiago-j-s/jev-proxy\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/a\u003e sits where stuntd sits\nand records every Jev request and answer to SQLite, with its latency, tokens and cost, for seven\ndays. It is a debugger rather than a learner: it trains nothing and answers nothing itself.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/dhruvmehra/jevbench\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003edhruvmehra/jevbench\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/a\u003e is the benchmark this README\nquotes for the zero-shot numbers. If you are choosing between Jev, Laya, an LLM and a fine-tuned\nBERT for your labels, run it first. stuntd's answer to \"Laya is worse than Jev on 77 labels\" is\nto train on your own data, but measuring comes first.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/yibie/awesome-jev\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eyibie/awesome-jev\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/a\u003e is the larger of the two catalogues\nof public Jev projects, integrations and discussions. A good place to check whether your decision\nis a pattern other people already run.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eNone of them learns from live traffic: recording the provider's own answers, a shadow phase, a\ncalibrated threshold and a fallback for everything under it is the loop stuntd adds. And every\nJev-compatible server above -- the laya-server family, kev, LLM2Jev -- can sit behind stuntd as\n\u003ccode\u003e[jev] upstream\u003c/code\u003e, which makes any of them a local teacher that needs no key.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eRoadmap\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eNext: support for new formats.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAdapters for Anthropic Messages, the OpenAI Responses API and Gemini, so those paths learn too.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eLater:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eLazy checkpoint load, so a daemon that serves nothing locally starts at once.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eEncode the state once per request instead of once per question, for multi-question latency.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eOption-order augmentation during training.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eDynamic candidate options, so a site whose option list changes does not need a new head.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eExport a trained site as a full Laya checkpoint.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eUnfreezing the top encoder layers, for decisions a frozen encoder cannot read.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003estuntd train\u003c/code\u003e on a schedule.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eContributing\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-contributing\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Contributing\" href=\"#contributing\"\u003e\u003csvg <p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/docs/cover.png"><img src="/bladedevoff/stuntd/raw/main/docs/cover.png" alt="stuntd: 90% of your LLM decisions answered locally, in about 20 ms, learned from your own traffic" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://github.com/bladedevoff/stuntd/actions/workflows/ci.yml"><img src="https://github.com/bladedevoff/stuntd/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg" alt="CI" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
<a href="https://pypi.org/project/stuntd/" rel="nofollow"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/08a3c0503fa23aef10b6b9acc27212585f1dd0d426814b4dc268ddb1b6da42d4/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f707970692f762f7374756e74642e737667" alt="PyPI" data-canonical-src="https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/stuntd.svg" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
<a href="/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/pyproject.toml"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/13466c63b4f964f1bc47e46eabb6ea9ebff2cb7777cba82af790a55719bbbfda/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f707974686f6e2d332e31302532422d626c75652e737667" alt="Python" data-canonical-src="https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
<a href="/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/LICENSE"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/798509b4df525f56802b56f8096862487f08023e3d7561c68656f8dab10d0d6e/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f6c6963656e73652d4170616368652d2d322e302d626c75652e737667" alt="License" data-canonical-src="https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
<a href="https://huggingface.co/spaces/pollix/stuntd" rel="nofollow"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/da1b8d14d75691a7c04f273fe01425ca03300e0d087ec920e27234bf69592d3c/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f484625323053706163652d74727925323069742d626c75652e737667" alt="Hugging Face Space" data-canonical-src="https://img.shields.io/badge/HF%20Space-try%20it-blue.svg" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>stuntd is a local, self-hosted proxy that records the typed decisions your app already makes and
learns to answer them itself.</strong> It speaks the Jev System One protocol (<code>POST /v1/systemone</code>, with
<code>choice</code>, <code>score</code> and <code>noul</code> questions) and the OpenAI Chat Completions API, distils each decision
site into a small head on a frozen <a href="https://huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya" rel="nofollow">Laya</a> encoder,
and serves that answer locally with calibrated confidence, handing anything it is unsure about back
to the provider.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Try it in the browser:</strong> the <a href="https://huggingface.co/spaces/pollix/stuntd" rel="nofollow">Hugging Face Space</a>
puts zero-shot Laya and the heads stuntd trained side by side on three demos, no install.</p>
<p dir="auto">Three ways to run it:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Local Jev.</strong> No key, no provider, no training. Point <code>typesafe-sdk</code> at stuntd and the base Laya
checkpoint answers your typed questions.</li>
<li><strong>In front of OpenAI.</strong> A drop-in replacement for the provider base URL. Typed requests are
recorded; everything else is relayed byte for byte.</li>
<li><strong>In front of the paid Jev API.</strong> stuntd relays, learns from the provider's own answers, and
takes the decision over once its head is right often enough.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Status: early release, v0.1. Every number below traces to a demo in this repository or to a source
listed at the end.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Who it is for</h2><a id="user-content-who-it-is-for" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Who it is for" href="#who-it-is-for"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>You have no Jev key.</strong> TypeSafe's Jev is an early-access API at the time of writing, and there
are no published weights. stuntd answers the same typed questions locally on Laya, with no key
and no training, so a <code>typesafe-sdk</code> client keeps working while you wait.</li>
<li><strong>You pay a provider for the same decision thousands of times a day.</strong> Routing, triage,
moderation, gating. stuntd distils those answers into a local head: tens of milliseconds, no
tokens, no round trip.</li>
<li><strong>Zero-shot Laya is not good enough on your labels.</strong> On banking77's 77 intents it scores 38.2
where Jev scores 76.4. A few thousand rows of your own traffic is what closes that gap: in the
banking demo the risk question goes from 30.0% to 72.5%.</li>
<li><strong>You want a Claude Code hook that decides locally.</strong> A <code>PreToolUse</code> gate answering "may this
command run" in about 50 ms, without sending every command you type to a provider.
<a href="/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/examples/devtools"><code>examples/devtools/</code></a> ships the hook.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Quickstart: local Jev without an API key</h2><a id="user-content-quickstart-local-jev-without-an-api-key" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Quickstart: local Jev without an API key" href="#quickstart-local-jev-without-an-api-key"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="pip install &quot;stuntd[train]&quot;
stuntd config init
stuntd serve"><pre class="notranslate"><code>pip install "stuntd[train]"
stuntd config init
stuntd serve
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>config init</code> writes a commented <code>stuntd.toml</code> with everything at its default, which means no
OpenAI upstream and no Jev provider. <code>serve</code> says so and loads the base checkpoint:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="stuntd listening on http://127.0.0.1:8787
no upstream: only the Jev routes are served
serving jev locally with convaiinnovations/laya"><pre class="notranslate"><code>stuntd listening on http://127.0.0.1:8787
no upstream: only the Jev routes are served
serving jev locally with convaiinnovations/laya
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Then change the base URL in your client and nothing else:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="from typesafe_sdk import Choice, Noul, TypeSafeClient

QUESTIONS = {
    &quot;category&quot;: Choice(
        instructions=&quot;Which part of the product is this ticket about?&quot;,
        criteria={&quot;billing&quot;: &quot;Payments and refunds.&quot;, &quot;bug&quot;: &quot;Something is broken.&quot;},
    ),
    &quot;needs_human&quot;: Noul(instructions=&quot;Does a support agent have to read this?&quot;),
}

with TypeSafeClient(api_key=&quot;local&quot;, base_url=&quot;http://127.0.0.1:8787&quot;) as client:
    answer = client.system_one(
        state={&quot;subject&quot;: &quot;Charged twice&quot;, &quot;body&quot;: &quot;Two identical charges on Friday.&quot;},
        questions=QUESTIONS,
    )
print(answer.choices[&quot;category&quot;].choice, answer.nouls[&quot;needs_human&quot;].noul)"><pre><span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">typesafe_sdk</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-v">Choice</span>, <span class="pl-v">Noul</span>, <span class="pl-v">TypeSafeClient</span>

<span class="pl-c1">QUESTIONS</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> {
    <span class="pl-s">"category"</span>: <span class="pl-en">Choice</span>(
        <span class="pl-s1">instructions</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"Which part of the product is this ticket about?"</span>,
        <span class="pl-s1">criteria</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span>{<span class="pl-s">"billing"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"Payments and refunds."</span>, <span class="pl-s">"bug"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"Something is broken."</span>},
    ),
    <span class="pl-s">"needs_human"</span>: <span class="pl-en">Noul</span>(<span class="pl-s1">instructions</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"Does a support agent have to read this?"</span>),
}

<span class="pl-k">with</span> <span class="pl-en">TypeSafeClient</span>(<span class="pl-s1">api_key</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"local"</span>, <span class="pl-s1">base_url</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"http://127.0.0.1:8787"</span>) <span class="pl-k">as</span> <span class="pl-s1">client</span>:
    <span class="pl-s1">answer</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">client</span>.<span class="pl-c1">system_one</span>(
        <span class="pl-s1">state</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span>{<span class="pl-s">"subject"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"Charged twice"</span>, <span class="pl-s">"body"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"Two identical charges on Friday."</span>},
        <span class="pl-s1">questions</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-c1">QUESTIONS</span>,
    )
<span class="pl-en">print</span>(<span class="pl-s1">answer</span>.<span class="pl-c1">choices</span>[<span class="pl-s">"category"</span>].<span class="pl-c1">choice</span>, <span class="pl-s1">answer</span>.<span class="pl-c1">nouls</span>[<span class="pl-s">"needs_human"</span>].<span class="pl-c1">noul</span>)</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Anything that speaks the protocol plugs in the same way, by changing one base URL wherever the
client exposes it: <code>typesafe-sdk</code>, JevRouter, the local-server request of fast-jev-compaction, and
the browser and game agents built on the same SDK.</p>
<p dir="auto">The key is ignored unless you set <code>[jev] require_key = true</code>. To train a head on this daemon you
need labelled rows: either put the paid Jev API in front of it (<code>[jev] upstream</code>) and let it teach,
or write the rows yourself and <code>stuntd import</code> them.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Quickstart: OpenAI-compatible proxy that learns</h2><a id="user-content-quickstart-openai-compatible-proxy-that-learns" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Quickstart: OpenAI-compatible proxy that learns" href="#quickstart-openai-compatible-proxy-that-learns"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="pip install &quot;stuntd[train]&quot;
stuntd config init
stuntd serve --upstream https://api.openai.com"><pre class="notranslate"><code>pip install "stuntd[train]"
stuntd config init
stuntd serve --upstream https://api.openai.com
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>--upstream</code> is the provider origin only, without <code>/v1</code>: your client's own path is appended to it
unchanged. In the client, point <code>base_url</code> at the daemon:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url=&quot;http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1&quot;, api_key=os.environ[&quot;OPENAI_API_KEY&quot;])"><pre><span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-s1">os</span>

<p dir="auto">Everything keeps working exactly as before. A request whose <code>response_format</code> (or single tool) asks
for an object with one enum, boolean or number field is a typed decision, and stuntd records it
with the provider's answer. Anything else is relayed untouched, streaming included.</p>
<p dir="auto">Once a site has a few hundred captures:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="stuntd status                  # what has been recorded, per site
stuntd train                   # one head per site with enough examples
stuntd report                  # holdout agreement, ECE, the operating point
stuntd enable &lt;site&gt;           # let that site answer locally"><pre class="notranslate"><code>stuntd status                  # what has been recorded, per site
stuntd train                   # one head per site with enough examples
stuntd report                  # holdout agreement, ECE, the operating point
stuntd enable &lt;site&gt;           # let that site answer locally
</code></pre></div>

<p dir="auto">Every decision site of the three text demos, measured against its teacher on held-out requests

<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/docs/before-after.svg"><img src="/bladedevoff/stuntd/raw/main/docs/before-after.svg" alt="Accuracy against the teacher, before and after training, per decision site" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto">Snake is scored by what the answers do rather than by how many of them are right:</p>
<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/docs/snake.svg"><img src="/bladedevoff/stuntd/raw/main/docs/snake.svg" alt="Snake average score over 30 games, zero-shot against the heads and the oracle" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto">Five of the seven sites in the three text demos reach a holdout agreement of 0.95 or better. The
demos run at the default <code>target_agreement</code> of 0.99, which picks each head's operating point rather
than being a score it reached. The two that fall short, support's <code>urgency</code> at 0.935 and banking's
<code>risk</code> at 0.937, stay in the demos anyway: see <a href="#limitations">limitations</a>.</p>

<p dir="auto">Zero-shot Laya holds its own at two or four labels and collapses at seventy-seven. A model trained
on a few thousand of your own examples does not: that is the bet stuntd makes, and the four demos
are what it is measured against.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">How stuntd distils decisions into a Laya head</h2><a id="user-content-how-stuntd-distils-decisions-into-a-laya-head" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: How stuntd distils decisions into a Laya head" href="#how-stuntd-distils-decisions-into-a-laya-head"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="   your app
      |
      v
  +-------------------------------------------------+
  |  stuntd                                          |
  |                                                  |

  |         |                                        |

      |
      v
  +-------------------------------------------------+
  |  stuntd                                          |
  |                                                  |
  |   typed decision?  -- no ---------------------------&gt;  provider, byte for byte
  |         |                                        |
  |        yes                                       |
  |         v                                        |
  |   head confident?  -- yes --&gt;  local answer      |     20 to 100 ms, no tokens
  |         |                                        |
  |         no, or a 2% check sample                 |
  +---------|----------------------------------------+
            v
        provider  (answer returned to the caller, and recorded as a capture)
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">A <strong>decision site</strong> is one place in your code that makes one decision. On the Jev path the site is
the question's name. On the OpenAI path it is a hash of the response schema and the system prompt,
or whatever you put in the <code>X-Stuntd-Site</code> request header.</p>
<p dir="auto">Keep one decision to a question. A question that mixes two, such as "is it urgent and which team
handles it", learns worse than two separate questions.</p>
<p dir="auto">Each site walks through four modes.</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><strong>collect.</strong> The provider answers everything. stuntd stores the request text and the answer,
with the redaction rules applied before anything is written.</li>
<li><strong>train.</strong> <code>stuntd train</code> fits one classification head per site on the frozen Laya encoder,
holds back 20% of the rows, and reports the holdout agreement, the calibration error and the
confidence threshold at which the head reaches your <code>target_agreement</code>:
<code>category  trained  holdout agreement 0.992  coverage 1.00 at agreement 0.992  ece 0.024</code>.
Below that threshold the head abstains, which is what coverage measures: the share of requests
it is willing to answer at all. <code>stuntd enable</code> refuses a head whose coverage rounds to zero and
warns below 10%.</li>
<li><strong>shadow.</strong> The caller still gets the provider's answer; the head answers beside it and the two
are compared. <code>stuntd status</code> shows the running agreement.</li>
<li><strong>live.</strong> <code>stuntd enable &lt;site&gt;</code> and the head answers the caller. Anything under the threshold
still goes to the provider. So does a <code>check_share</code> sample, 2% by default, and those samples are
what keeps the head honest: once agreement over the last <code>window</code> decisions falls below
<code>target_agreement</code>, the site demotes itself back to shadow and logs why. Promotion the other way
is manual unless you set <code>serving.auto_promote</code>.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">In proxy mode the provider behind <code>[jev] upstream</code> does not have to be the paid API. Any server
that speaks <code>POST /v1/systemone</code> can sit there -- kev, LLM2Jev, the laya-server family -- which
makes it a keyless local teacher: it answers, stuntd records, and the head learns from it.</p>
<p dir="auto">Nothing is uploaded. Captures live in a SQLite file under your user directory with private
permissions, and there is no telemetry.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Checking a head against verified rows</h3><a id="user-content-checking-a-head-against-verified-rows" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Checking a head against verified rows" href="#checking-a-head-against-verified-rows"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Agreement measures how faithfully a head copies its teacher, the teacher's mistakes included. It
says nothing about whether either of them is right. For that, write a few hundred rows a person
has checked, in the same JSONL format <code>stuntd import</code> reads, and score the site against them:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="stuntd report &lt;site&gt; --gold verified.jsonl"><pre class="notranslate"><code>stuntd report &lt;site&gt; --gold verified.jsonl
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">For example:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="site tickets  gold rows 300: 296 used, 4 skipped
head accuracy 0.892
head accuracy 0.875 on 8 rows the store has not seen
served accuracy 0.936 at threshold 0.62: 71% answered locally, 3 below it with no teacher answer
teacher accuracy 0.948 on 288 rows
head and teacher: both right 252, both wrong 10, head only 5, teacher only 21"><pre class="notranslate"><code>site tickets  gold rows 300: 296 used, 4 skipped
head accuracy 0.892
head accuracy 0.875 on 8 rows the store has not seen
served accuracy 0.936 at threshold 0.62: 71% answered locally, 3 below it with no teacher answer
teacher accuracy 0.948 on 288 rows
head and teacher: both right 252, both wrong 10, head only 5, teacher only 21
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The head answers every row. The teacher's answer is the latest capture of that exact text, so it
is there only for rows stuntd has already seen, and those are rows the head may have trained on.
The line for rows the store has not seen is the out-of-sample number, so do not import the gold
rows or send them through the proxy before scoring. Served accuracy is what stuntd would serve
once the site is live: the head at or above the threshold, the teacher below it. Rows whose answer
is not one of the site's labels are skipped. <code>--json</code> prints the same numbers, and the command needs the train
extra, since it loads the base model.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The <code>X-Stuntd</code> header</h3><a id="user-content-the-x-stuntd-header" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The X-Stuntd header" href="#the-x-stuntd-header"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Every answer says how it was served, so a silent fallback cannot hide.</p>
