<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Configuration</h2><a id="user-content-configuration" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Configuration" href="#configuration"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>stuntd config init</code> writes the file; <code>stuntd config show</code> prints every setting with where it came
from. Every key is optional and a missing one keeps the default.</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>key</th>
<th>default</th>
<th>what it does</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>upstream</code></td>
<td><code>""</code></td>
<td>Provider origin the OpenAI path forwards to, no path. Empty: only the Jev routes are served.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>host</code></td>
<td><code>127.0.0.1</code></td>
<td>Address the daemon listens on.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>port</code></td>
<td><code>8787</code></td>
<td>Port the daemon listens on.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>learn</code></td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>Whether the daemon records anything at all. <code>false</code> is a pure proxy, or a pure local Jev.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>redaction.enabled</code></td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>Built-in email and phone rules run before a capture is written.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>redaction.patterns</code></td>
<td><code>[]</code></td>
<td>Extra regular expressions, each replaced with <code>[redacted]</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>storage.db_path</code></td>
<td><code>captures.sqlite</code></td>
<td>Capture database; a relative path resolves against the data directory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>storage.max_rows</code></td>
<td><code>100000</code></td>
<td>Captures kept before the oldest are pruned.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>storage.max_age_days</code></td>
<td><code>30</code></td>
<td>Age at which a capture is pruned.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>storage.models_dir</code></td>
<td><code>models</code></td>
<td>Where trained heads live.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>training.min_examples</code></td>
<td><code>300</code></td>
<td>Captures a site needs before it is worth training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>training.holdout</code></td>
<td><code>0.2</code></td>
<td>Share of the rows held back to measure the head.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>training.target_agreement</code></td>
<td><code>0.99</code></td>
<td>Agreement with the teacher the head must reach; it sets the confidence threshold.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>training.base_model</code></td>
<td><code>convaiinnovations/laya</code></td>
<td>Checkpoint the heads are trained on. A local directory works too.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>training.epochs</code></td>
<td><code>3</code></td>
<td>Passes over the training rows. The demos use 24.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>training.device</code></td>
<td><code>auto</code></td>
<td><code>auto</code>, <code>cpu</code>, <code>cuda</code> or <code>mps</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>training.cache_encoder</code></td>
<td><code>true</code></td>
<td>Whether the frozen encoder runs once per example instead of once per epoch; off re-encodes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>training.cache_max_mb</code></td>
<td><code>0</code></td>
<td>Most memory the cached encoder output may take, in megabytes; 0 is half of physical memory. A bigger site trains uncached and says so on stderr.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>training.max_option_tokens</code></td>
<td><code>1024</code></td>
<td>How far a site with many or long labels may widen the option budget, in tokens, so every label is shown whole; past it, labels are cut short. A value below the checkpoint's own budget (192) keeps the checkpoint's.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>serving.check_share</code></td>
<td><code>0.02</code></td>
<td>Share of live requests still sent to the provider to check the head. Inert in local Jev mode.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>serving.window</code></td>
<td><code>100</code></td>
<td>Recent decisions a site is judged on.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>serving.min_window</code></td>
<td><code>20</code></td>
<td>Decisions needed before that judgement counts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>serving.auto_promote</code></td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>Whether a shadow site that holds its target goes live on its own.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>serving.auto_promote_after_hours</code></td>
<td><code>24</code></td>
<td>Hours in shadow before it may.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>serving.cache_size</code></td>
<td><code>1000</code></td>
<td>Answers kept in memory, one LRU cache shared by every site.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev.upstream</code></td>
<td><code>""</code></td>
<td>Origin of the paid Jev provider, no path. Empty: the base Laya answers locally.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev.require_key</code></td>
<td><code>false</code></td>
<td>Whether a Jev request must carry a Bearer token. The token itself is not checked.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jev.model_name</code></td>
<td><code>stuntd</code></td>
<td>Name reported in the <code>model</code> field of a Jev answer.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Demos</h2><a id="user-content-demos" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Demos" href="#demos"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Four runnable demos, each with its own README, its own generated data and its own measured table.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/docs/snake-demo.gif"><img src="/bladedevoff/stuntd/raw/main/docs/snake-demo.gif" alt="Snake played three ways over the Jev protocol: base Laya zero-shot, the BFS teacher, and the head stuntd trained from the teacher's games" data-animated-image="" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto">Same seed, same <code>typesafe-sdk</code> client, same daemon. Left: the base Laya checkpoint answering
zero-shot. Middle: the BFS oracle that plays teacher. Right: the head stuntd trained from the
teacher's 30 games (138 s), answering 99.6% of the moves itself at 20 ms each. Numbers and
commands are in <a href="/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/examples/snake">examples/snake/</a>.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><a href="/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/examples/snake"><code>examples/snake/</code></a> plays 12x12 Snake over the Jev protocol, one <code>choice</code> per
move. Zero-shot Laya scores 0.70 a game; the head scores 11.40 at <code>target_agreement = 0.95</code>,
answering all but 13 of 3050 moves locally at a p50 of 21.1 ms. At the default 0.99 the same head
scores 3.03 and answers 71% of the moves. That is the difference between "let the head play" and "only when
it is sure", in one table.</li>
<li><a href="/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/examples/support"><code>examples/support/</code></a> triages a helpdesk ticket with three questions in one
request: <code>category</code> (choice), <code>urgency</code> (score) and <code>needs_human</code> (noul). 90% of the questions
end up answered locally.</li>
<li><a href="/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/examples/banking"><code>examples/banking/</code></a> asks a banking intent over 12 labels and a payment risk
verdict. 78% local, and <code>intent</code> reaches a holdout agreement of 1.000.</li>
<li><a href="/bladedevoff/stuntd/blob/main/examples/devtools"><code>examples/devtools/</code></a> gates a coding agent's shell command and calls a test
failure flaky. 98% local, and it ships the Claude Code <code>PreToolUse</code> hook that uses it.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>The teachers in all four are rules, not an LLM.</strong> Three demos use a written rule over the
generated text; Snake uses a BFS oracle. No Jev API key was available when these numbers were
taken, so the zero-shot rows are the base checkpoint, not the paid provider, and the same tables
with the real Jev API as the teacher have not been measured yet. What the demos do show is what a
head learns from a teacher that is consistent: the ceiling of the method, not of any one provider.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Limitations</h2><a id="user-content-limitations" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Limitations" href="#limitations"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>The encoder is frozen, so a head learns text, not arithmetic over fields.</strong> This is the single
most important thing to know. In the banking demo the first version of the <code>risk</code> rule compared the
amount, the country and the hour numerically: the head reached 0.42 and covered 1% of the holdout.
The same decision, written as a sentence about the customer's own history, reaches 0.937 at
coverage 0.57. If your decision is really a calculation, write the calculation, not a model.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Free text is not a decision.</strong> stuntd learns closed decisions only: an enum, a boolean or a
number on the OpenAI path, <code>choice</code>, <code>noul</code> or <code>score</code> on the Jev path. A request that asks for
prose, a summary or code is relayed and never recorded.</li>
<li><strong>A site needs examples.</strong> <code>training.min_examples</code> is 300 and the demos use 3000 rows. A rare
decision, or one whose option list changes every week, is not a fit.</li>
<li><strong>Overlapping labels make a head defer.</strong> The weakest site of the three text demos is the
support demo's <code>urgency</code>, a four-level <code>score</code>. Its levels overlap in wording, so the head
reaches a 0.935 holdout agreement and answers 71% of the tickets at 99.1% agreement, handing the
other 29% to the provider. That is a working site rather than a failure, but it is the shape to
expect when the labels are not cleanly separated by words.</li>
<li><strong>Only the OpenAI Chat Completions path learns.</strong> Anthropic Messages, the OpenAI Responses API
and Gemini pass through untouched. Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI run through stuntd as if
it were not there.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Details worth knowing</h3><a id="user-content-details-worth-knowing" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Details worth knowing" href="#details-worth-knowing"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Some decisions need more than the default 3 epochs.</strong> The default stays 3, and the demos
train at 24 because each of them measured what that bought. The frozen encoder runs once per
site and every epoch reads its cached output, so the extra epochs cost seconds, not minutes.
At 3 epochs the same sites answer almost nothing.</li>
<li><strong><code>score</code> takes 2 to 10 levels and <code>choice</code> takes at most 255 options.</strong> Those are stuntd's own
limits, not a quotation from the Jev API. <code>instructions</code> is optional on a question.</li>
<li><strong>A question name is a decision site.</strong> <code>:</code> becomes <code>.</code>, so <code>a:b</code> and <code>a.b</code> are one site. Two
questions with the same name but different criteria train one head on mixed data; give them
different names.</li>
<li><strong><code>GET /v1/models</code> is answered by stuntd</strong>, in the Jev shape, naming <code>jev.model_name</code>. In proxy
mode it is relayed to the Jev provider. Either way an OpenAI client does not get the provider's
model list through stuntd; every other <code>/v1/models...</code> path is relayed as usual.</li>
<li><strong>Local Jev mode compares nothing.</strong> There is no second opinion to compare against, because the
zero-shot answers come from the very checkpoint the head was distilled from. No request is
sampled for a check, <code>stuntd status</code> reports <code>"agreement": null</code>, and no site is ever demoted.
<code>stuntd report</code>, which measures the head against held-out rows, is the quality signal there. Put
a Jev provider in front and both come back.</li>
<li><strong>One CUDA workload at a time.</strong> Stop the daemon before <code>stuntd train</code>, or the two contend for
the same GPU.</li>
<li><strong>Every <code>serve</code> loads the base checkpoint</strong> when <code>[jev] upstream</code> is empty, because local Jev
answers from it. The daemon runs one pass through the model before it accepts requests, so
startup costs seconds and the first request then runs close to the steady-state p50. Lazy
loading is on the roadmap.</li>
<li><strong>The first start needs the network.</strong> <code>serve</code> and <code>train</code> load <code>training.base_model</code>, which
defaults to the Hub id, so the first run downloads the whole repository, the <code>multilingual/</code>
and <code>typed-decisions/</code> checkpoints included. With <code>HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1</code> the Hub id loads only
while that whole snapshot is in the Hugging Face cache; a partial one fails. For fully offline
use, set <code>training.base_model</code> to a local directory holding the checkpoint, such as the
snapshot folder.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Compared with</h2><a id="user-content-compared-with" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Compared with" href="#compared-with"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><a href="https://github.com/stiermid/laya-serve"><strong>stiermid/laya-serve</strong></a> is a Jev-compatible HTTP server
for Laya weights. It is the cleaner choice when zero-shot is all you want: it documents its
divergences from the Jev wire format carefully, and it carries no database, no training and no
proxy. stuntd's local mode does the same job; what it adds is learning from traffic.</li>
<li>The rest of the laya-server family serves those weights behind the same API:
<a href="https://github.com/noahbclarkson/laya-server">noahbclarkson/laya-server</a> ships a container, a
health endpoint and TypeSafe's error shapes, <a href="https://github.com/receptron/laya">receptron/laya</a>
runs Laya from Node through ONNX Runtime. All of them answer zero-shot only.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/jaredpalmer/kev"><strong>jaredpalmer/kev</strong></a> trains Jev-like decision models on
Qwen3.5 and publishes the weights at 0.8B, 4B and 9B, with the training code, frozen eval suites
and a System One API in front of them. A whole model per decision, where stuntd trains one head
per site on a frozen encoder.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/Yinsongxu/LLM2Jev"><strong>Yinsongxu/LLM2Jev</strong></a> puts local LLMs behind
<code>/v1/systemone</code> and scores each option during the prefill, so reordering the options does not
change the answer. stuntd has neither that order independence nor its image inputs; what it has
is a head that answers without the LLM.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/TheoLeeCJ/SemIf"><strong>TheoLeeCJ/SemIf</strong></a> reads typed option probabilities
straight out of open 4B models, with a browser demo and no waitlist. It reproduces the interface
rather than the model, and every decision still costs a pass through the 4B.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/TianyuCodings/NanoJev"><strong>TianyuCodings/NanoJev</strong></a> trains a 0.6B decision
model from prepared game datasets and plays ViZDoom, a maze and Snake with the one checkpoint.
Its Snake comes from a model trained for the game; stuntd's comes from a head distilled from
5890 recorded moves of a BFS oracle.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/vinnylarouge/jevlike"><strong>vinnylarouge/jevlike</strong></a> trains an option-attention
head from JSONL rows of a context, its options and a label. That is <code>stuntd train</code> as a
standalone library: you bring the rows, and nothing records them for you.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/gargpratyush/jev-router"><strong>gargpratyush/jev-router</strong></a> uses Jev to pick a
model tier per turn for Claude Code and Codex. A different problem, and a good example of the
decision stuntd would learn: a routing call on every turn is exactly the repeated typed decision
that pays for a head.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/Santiago-j-s/jev-proxy"><strong>Santiago-j-s/jev-proxy</strong></a> sits where stuntd sits
and records every Jev request and answer to SQLite, with its latency, tokens and cost, for seven
days. It is a debugger rather than a learner: it trains nothing and answers nothing itself.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/dhruvmehra/jevbench"><strong>dhruvmehra/jevbench</strong></a> is the benchmark this README
quotes for the zero-shot numbers. If you are choosing between Jev, Laya, an LLM and a fine-tuned
BERT for your labels, run it first. stuntd's answer to "Laya is worse than Jev on 77 labels" is
to train on your own data, but measuring comes first.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/yibie/awesome-jev"><strong>yibie/awesome-jev</strong></a> is the larger of the two catalogues
of public Jev projects, integrations and discussions. A good place to check whether your decision
is a pattern other people already run.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">None of them learns from live traffic: recording the provider's own answers, a shadow phase, a
calibrated threshold and a fallback for everything under it is the loop stuntd adds. And every
Jev-compatible server above -- the laya-server family, kev, LLM2Jev -- can sit behind stuntd as
<code>[jev] upstream</code>, which makes any of them a local teacher that needs no key.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Roadmap</h2><a id="user-content-roadmap" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Roadmap" href="#roadmap"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Next: support for new formats.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Adapters for Anthropic Messages, the OpenAI Responses API and Gemini, so those paths learn too.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Later:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Lazy checkpoint load, so a daemon that serves nothing locally starts at once.</li>
<li>Encode the state once per request instead of once per question, for multi-question latency.</li>
<li>Option-order augmentation during training.</li>
<li>Dynamic candidate options, so a site whose option list changes does not need a new head.</li>
<li>Export a trained site as a full Laya checkpoint.</li>
<li>Unfreezing the top encoder layers, for decisions a frozen encoder cannot read.</li>
<li><code>stuntd train</code> on a schedule.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Contributing</h2><a id="user-content-contributing" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Contributing" href="#contributing"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<li>Jev pricing, context limit and model sheet:
<a href="https://docs.typesafe.ai/models" rel="nofollow">docs.typesafe.ai/models</a>. $0.042 per 1M input tokens, output

<li>Zero-shot accuracy and API latency: <a href="https://github.com/dhruvmehra/jevbench">dhruvmehra/jevbench</a>,
the run of 2026-09-22, n=500 per dataset

<li>Jev wire format and its documented divergences from Laya:
<a href="https://github.com/stiermid/laya-serve">stiermid/laya-serve</a>.</li>
<li>Head latency, relay overhead and head size: measured during development on an RTX 5060 laptop
running Windows. Not public, so there is no link.</li>
<li>Every other stuntd number: the four demo READMEs linked above, each of which states the
hardware, the row count and the epochs it was measured at.</li>
</ul>
